user_query: My Base Sum Insured got fully used up by a claim earlier this policy year. If I'm hospitalized again this year, will Super Reload pay, and how much at most?
ground_truth_response: Yes, provided the conditions are met. Super Reload is triggered when the Base Sum Insured plus any accumulated Super Credit is exhausted or insufficient, and reloads an amount equal to the Base Sum Insured, unlimited times in the Policy Year. It is not payable for the first claim in the life of the Policy, but is payable for all subsequent claims, so a second claim qualifies. The claim must be admissible under Section C.1, C.5, C.6, C.7 or C.8, and the maximum liability under a single claim under Super Reload is the Base Sum Insured. Accumulated Super Credit is used before Super Reload.
verbatim_context: If the Base Sum Insured along with accumulated Super Credit (if applicable) for the Policy Year in respect of the Insured Person, is completely exhausted or is insufficient for covering a claim, then We shall provide for a reload amounting to the Base Sum Insured (“Super Reload”), unlimited times during the Policy Year [...] The Super Reload shall not become payable to the first claim in the life of the Policy [...] Our total, maximum liability under a single claim under this Benefit shall not be more than the Base Sum Insured. [...] Base Sum Insured followed by; b. Super Credit (if inbuilt / opted and applicable) followed by; c. Super Reload followed by;
source_reference: Appendix A, Section C.10 Super Reload (Page 31); Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (Page 46)

user_query: What are the notification and pre-authorization timelines for a planned cashless hospitalization versus an emergency one?
ground_truth_response: Planned: notice must be given at least 48 hours prior to admission, and it is advisable to contact the insurer to pre-authorise Cashless Facility at least 72 hours prior to the proposed treatment. Emergency: notice must be given within 24 hours of emergency Hospitalization or before discharge, whichever is earlier, and pre-authorisation must be requested within 24 hours of Hospitalization. In both cases the initial authorization letter is issued to the Network Provider within one hour of receiving complete information; once granted, treatment must take place within 15 days of the pre-authorization date.

user_query: If I'm diagnosed with a covered critical illness, when do I have to inform the insurer, when are documents due, and when is the lump sum payable?

Claim documents must be submitted within 30 days of the event (the earliest of first diagnosis / surgical procedure / medical event). The Sum Insured is payable for an illness first diagnosed during the Policy Period after completion of 60 days from the Commencement Date, subject to the Insured Person surviving 15 days following the first diagnosis/surgical procedure.
verbatim_context: You or anyone on behalf of the Insured Person(s) shall intimate a claim to Us within 7 days from the date of the Accident or diagnosis of the Critical Illness or admission in the Hospital (as the case may be) [...] shall submit the following documents within 30 (thirty) days of the earliest of the date of first diagnosis of the Critical Illness/ date of Surgical Procedure or date of occurrence of the medical event [...] We shall pay the Sum Insured as mentioned in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table for that Critical Illness after completion of 60 days from the Commencement Date [...] subject to survival of the Insured Person for 15 days following the first diagnosis

user_query: I have the Personal Accident cover with a 20 lakh sum insured. If I permanently lose my thumb (both phalanges) in an accident, how much would I get?
ground_truth_response: Under Permanent Partial Disability, loss of thumb (both phalanges) is payable at 25% of the Sum Insured. With a Personal Accident Sum Insured of INR 20 Lacs (an available option), 25% equals INR 5,00,000.
verbatim_context: Loss of thumb [...] - both phalanges 25% [...] We will pay a percentage of the Sum Insured as per the below table [...] Base Sum Insured Options - INR 10 Lacs, INR 15 Lacs, INR 20 Lacs, INR 25 Lacs,

user_query: If my policy covers treatment outside India and I want planned treatment abroad, how does the process work and what won't be paid?
ground_truth_response: Treatment outside India is excluded unless specified as covered in the Policy Schedule. Where covered, for planned treatment the insurer/Empanelled Service Provider identifies 3 Hospitals; after the Insured Person confirms treatment abroad, 3 hospitals in the chosen country are identified (or a fourth option from the network may be chosen). The insurer arranges logistics and issues a Preliminary Medical Certificate valid only for that Hospital. Expenses in a different Hospital, or incurred before the Preliminary Medical Certificate is issued, are not covered. The recommended hospital list and Preliminary Medical Certificate are valid for three months.
verbatim_context: Treatment taken outside India, unless specified to be covered in the Policy Schedule. [...] We / Our Empanelled Service Provider will identify 3 Hospitals from Our network. [...] will issue a Preliminary Medical Certificate valid only for that Hospital. [...] Any expense incurred in a different Hospital from the one specified in the Preliminary Medical Certificate will not be covered. [...] Any expense incurred before the issuance of the Preliminary Medical Certificate will not be covered. [...] both documents will have a validity of three months.

user_query: I have Type 2 diabetes and opted for the Chronic Management Program (OPD). What consultations and tests do I get, and where?
ground_truth_response: For Diabetes Type 2 (single condition), you are entitled to 1 Teleconsult - Physician, 1 Teleconsult - Endocrinologist, 1 Onboarding Physical HA (BMI / BP / RR / HR / HBA1C / Lipid Profile / Creatinine), and 1 Follow-up 6 months later (HBA1C / Lipid / BP / Heart Rate). The program is for Insured Persons aged 18 and above and is available only on a Cashless Facility basis at Network Providers and Empanelled Service Providers.

user_query: If I'm admitted to an AYUSH hospital, are pre- and post-hospitalization costs covered, and what can HealthReturns be used for in relation to AYUSH?
ground_truth_response: AYUSH In-patient Care in an AYUSH Hospital or AYUSH Day Care Centre is covered at actuals up to Sum Insured. Pre-hospitalization (90 days) and post-hospitalization (180 days) expenses are covered for admissible hospitalization under Section C.7 (AYUSH Treatment). HealthReturns can be used for AYUSH Treatments in excess of the limits specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table; such reimbursement claims can be submitted quarterly.

[...] AYUSH Treatment Actuals up to Sum Insured [...] Section C.7 (AYUSH Treatment) for up to 90 days immediately prior to the date of such Hospitalization. user_query: I pay my premium monthly. If I make a claim mid-year, what happens to my remaining instalments, and could I get a refund if I cancel later?
ground_truth_response: In the event of a claim, all subsequent premium instalments immediately become due and payable, and the Company has the right to recover and deduct all pending instalments from the claim amount. For instalment policies with an admissible claim, future instalments for the current Policy Year are adjusted in the claim amount and no premium is refunded during the Policy Year. In any case, no refund is applicable on cancellation for Half Yearly, Quarterly and Monthly premium frequencies, and no refund is made where any claim has been admitted or lodged.
verbatim_context: ln the event of a claim, all subsequent premium instalments shall immediately become due and payable [...] The Company has the right to recover and deduct all the pending instalments from the claim amount due under the Policy. [...] No refund is applicable for Half Yearly, Quarterly & Monthly premium frequencies. [...] no refunds of premium shall be made in respect of Cancellation where, any claim has been admitted or has been lodged or any benefit has been availed by the Insured Person under the Policy.
source_reference: Section E.1.17 Premium Payment in Instalments (Pages 18-19); Section E.1.2 Cancellation (Page 15)

user_query: Am I covered if I'm hospitalized during the grace period after my policy expired?
ground_truth_response: It depends on the premium payment mode, and the document contains differing statements. Section E.1.3 (Renewal) states that coverage is not available during the grace period. However, for premiums paid in instalments (Half Yearly, Quarterly or Monthly), Section E.1.17 states the Policy remains in force during the grace period and claims arising during it are payable subject to policy terms; the Grace Period definition likewise says coverage is available during the Grace Period if premium is paid in instalments during the Policy Period. So for annual/one-time renewals there is no cover during the grace period; for instalment premiums, cover continues during the instalment grace period.
verbatim_context: Coverage is not available during the grace period. [...] The Policy will be in force during such grace period and any claims arising during the Grace Period will be payable subject to policy terms and conditions. [...] Coverage is available during the Grace Period, if the premium is paid in instalments during the Policy Period
source_reference: Section E.1.3 Renewal of Policy iv (Page 16); Section E.1.17 b) (Page 18); Section B.1 Definition 23 - Grace Period (Page 3)

user_query: What's the deadline for submitting a post-hospitalization reimbursement claim?
ground_truth_response: The document gives two different timelines. The prescribed time-limit table in Section E.2.7 states reimbursement of Post Hospitalization Expenses must be made within 15 days from completion of post-hospitalization treatment. Section E.2.7.1 e) i. states claims for Pre- and Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses are to be submitted within 30 days of completion of the post-hospitalization treatment. A RAG system should surface both and recommend submitting within the shorter 15-day window. Delays may be condoned on merit where proved to be for reasons beyond the Insured Person's control.
verbatim_context: Reimbursement of Post Hospitalization Expenses Within 15 days from completion of post Hospitalization treatment. [...] Claims for Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses and Post Hospitalization Medical Expenses to be submitted to us within 30 days of the completion of the post hospitalization treatment [...] Any delay in notification or submission may be condoned on merit where delay is proved to be for reasons beyond the control of the Insured Person
source_reference: Section E.2.7 Claims - Prescribed Time Limit table (Page 20); Section E.2.7.1 e) Claims Documentation (Page 22); Section E.2.7 b) Note (Page 21)

user_query: Is an injury from recreational scuba diving on holiday excluded under the hazardous sports exclusion, or only if I'm a professional diver?
ground_truth_response: The Hazardous or Adventure sports exclusion (Excl09) is worded to exclude expenses for treatment necessitated due to participation 'as a professional' in hazardous or adventure sports, including scuba diving. The exclusion text does not extend to non-professional participation. Note that the separate definition of Adventure/Hazardous Sports in Section B.2 covers participation for entertainment or as a profession, trained or not, but the operative exclusion clause is limited to professional participation.
verbatim_context: Expenses related to any treatment necessitated due to participation as a professional in hazardous or adventure sports, including but not limited to, para-jumping, rock climbing, mountaineering, rafting, motor racing, horse racing or scuba diving, hand gliding, sky diving, deep sea diving [...] in which an Insured Person participates or competes for entertainment or as part of his profession whether he / she is trained or not.
source_reference: Section D.1.9 Hazardous or Adventure sports (Code-Excl09) (Page 12); Section B.2 Specific Definitions, Definition 1 (Page 5)

user_query: Is treatment for a congenital anomaly covered? Does it matter whether it's internal or external?
ground_truth_response: Yes, it matters. The Medical Exclusions exclude any conditions or abnormalities present at birth that are visible on the outside of the body, and related diseases or defects, which corresponds to an External Congenital Anomaly (in the visible and accessible parts of the body). The exclusion text does not refer to Internal Congenital Anomalies (not in the visible and accessible parts of the body); those are not excluded by this clause, though other terms such as Pre-Existing Disease waiting periods still apply.
verbatim_context: Internal Congenital Anomaly [...] Congenital anomaly which is not in the visible and accessible parts of the body. [...] External Congenital Anomaly [...] Congenital anomaly which is in the visible and accessible parts of the body. [...] Any conditions or abnormalities that are present at birth and are visible on the outside of the body, as well as any related diseases or defects,
source_reference: Section B.1 Definition 9 - Congenital Anomaly (Page 2); Section D.2.3 Medical Exclusions f) (Page 13)

user_query: Is plastic or cosmetic surgery ever covered?
ground_truth_response: Cosmetic or plastic surgery or treatment to change appearance is excluded, unless it is for reconstruction following an Accident, Burn(s) or Cancer, or is part of medically necessary treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured, which must be certified by the attending Medical Practitioner. Separately, Plastic Surgery medically necessitated due to Injury is listed as a covered expense under hospitalization.
verbatim_context: Expenses for cosmetic or plastic surgery or any treatment to change appearance unless for reconstruction following an Accident, Burn(s) or Cancer or as part of medically necessary treatment to remove a direct and immediate health risk to the insured. For this to be considered a medical necessity, it must be certified by the attending Medical Practitioner. [...] Plastic Surgery, medically necessitated due to Injury.
source_reference: Section D.1.8 Cosmetic or plastic Surgery (Code-Excl08) (Page 12); Appendix A, Section C.1.1.1 c (Page 29)

user_query: What conditions must be met for bariatric (obesity) surgery to be covered?
ground_truth_response: Obesity Treatment (Bariatric Surgery) during Hospitalization is covered at actuals up to Sum Insured, subject to all conditions in Excl06: (a) surgery is on the advice of the Doctor; (b) the surgery/procedure is supported by clinical protocols; (c) the member is 18 years of age or older; and (d) BMI is greater than or equal to 40, or greater than or equal to 35 with any of these severe co-morbidities following failure of less invasive weight loss methods: obesity-related cardiomyopathy, coronary heart disease, severe sleep apnea, or uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes.
verbatim_context: Obesity Treatment: Medical Expenses incurred towards treatment taken by the Insured Person during Hospitalization Treatment under Section C.1 of the Insured Person arising out of Hospitalization for a Bariatric Surgery [...] Surgery to be conducted is upon the advice of the Doctor. [...] The surgery / Procedure conducted should be supported by clinical protocols. [...] The member has to be 18 years of age or older and [...] greater than or equal to 40 or [...] greater than or equal to 35 in conjunction with any of the following severe co-morbidities following failure of less invasive methods of weight loss:
source_reference: Appendix A, Section C.1.1.1 h (Page 29); Section D.1.6 Obesity / Weight Control (Code- Excl06) (Pages 11-12)

user_query: I want LASIK to fix my eyesight. Is refractive error correction covered?
ground_truth_response: Treatment for correction of eyesight due to refractive error of less than 7.5 dioptres is permanently excluded. Refractive Error Correction surgery is also on the specified disease/procedure list, so even where the refractive error is 7.5 dioptres or more, it is subject to the 24-month specific waiting period (unless due to an accident). Separately, Femto Laser Surgeries are listed under Specific treatment exclusions.
verbatim_context: Expenses related to the treatment for correction of eye sight due to refractive error less than 7.5 dioptres. [...] Refractive Error Correction Correction Surgery [...] Femto Laser Surgeries
source_reference: Section D.1.15 Refractive Error (Code-Excl15) (Page 12); Section D.1.2 f) list (Page 10); Section D.2.6 Specific treatment Exclusion (Page 14)

user_query: Is dental treatment covered?
ground_truth_response: Generally dental/oral treatment related to natural teeth and gingiva is excluded, except if required by an Insured Person while Hospitalized due to an Accident. Additionally, Section C.1.1.1 lists Dental Treatment under Inpatient Care, medically necessitated due to Illness or Injury, as a covered expense. Out-patient dental treatment is not covered.
verbatim_context: Dental / Oral Treatment: Treatment, procedures and preventive, diagnostic, restor [...] ative, cosmetic services related to disease, disorder and conditions related to natural teeth and gingiva except if required by an Insured Person while Hospitalized due to an Accident [...] Dental Treatment under Inpatient Care, medically necessitated due to Illness or Injury.
source_reference: Section D.2.3 Medical Exclusions h) (Page 13); Appendix A, Section C.1.1.1 b (Page 29)

user_query: Are pregnancy complications covered — specifically an ectopic pregnancy or a miscarriage?
ground_truth_response: Maternity expenses traceable to childbirth (including complicated deliveries and caesarean sections) are excluded, except ectopic pregnancy, which is therefore not excluded by this clause. Expenses towards miscarriage are excluded unless the miscarriage is due to an accident. Lawful medical termination of pregnancy is excluded.
verbatim_context: Medical treatment expenses traceable to childbirth (including complicated deliveries and caesarean sections incurred during hospitalization) except ectopic pregnancy; [...] Expenses towards miscarriage (unless due to an accident) and lawful medical termination of pregnancy during the policy period

user_query: What happens if I'm admitted to a hospital that the insurer has excluded?
ground_truth_response: Expenses at a hospital or provider specifically excluded by the insurer (as disclosed on its website or notified to policyholders) are not admissible. However, in life-threatening situations or following an accident, expenses up to the stage of stabilization are payable, but not the complete claim. Note that Section C.4 states the Excluded Providers exclusion does not apply to the Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver) cover.
verbatim_context: Expenses incurred towards treatment in any hospital or by any Medical Practitioner or any other provider specifically excluded by the Insurer as disclosed in website [...] However, in case of life threatening situations or following an accident, expenses up to the stage of stabilization are payable but not the complete claim. user_query: My spouse is a doctor. If she treats me, can I claim for it?
ground_truth_response: Not by default. A Medical Practitioner who shares the same residence as the Insured Person and is a Family Member is not considered a Medical Practitioner under the Policy. Treatments provided by a Medical Practitioner who is a family member or resides in the same household are excluded, unless pre-approval is obtained from the insurer.

[...] Treatments provided by a Medical Practitioner who is a family member of the Insured Person or resides in the same household, unless pre-approval is obtained from Us.

user_query: I ported to this policy from another insurer where I had 3 years of continuous cover. Does the 30-day initial waiting period still apply to me?
ground_truth_response: No. The 30-day waiting period exclusion does not apply if the Insured Person has Continuous Coverage for more than twelve months. It would, however, apply to any enhanced sum insured granted subsequently. Portability also reduces the PED and specific disease waiting periods to the extent of prior coverage.

[...] The within referred Waiting Period is made applicable to the enhanced sum insured in the event of granting higher sum insured subsequently. user_query: I had kidney stones diagnosed a year before buying the policy. Which waiting period applies — 2 years or 3 years?
ground_truth_response: Stones in the urinary system (kidney, ureter, urinary bladder) are on the specified disease list (2-year waiting period). Because the condition was diagnosed before the policy started, it is also a Pre-Existing Disease (3-year waiting period). Where a specified disease falls under the PED waiting period, the longer of the two applies, so the 3-year PED waiting period applies (unless reduced via the optional PED reduction cover or portability credit). It must also have been declared and accepted.
verbatim_context: Stones in Urinary System [...] (Stone in the Kidney, Ureter, Urinary Bladder) [...] If any of the specified disease / procedure falls under the Waiting Period specified for pre-existing diseases, then the longer of the two Waiting Periods shall apply. user_query: Can I claim Cancer Booster on a cashless basis, and how many times per year?
ground_truth_response: No, Cancer Booster expenses can be claimed on a reimbursement basis only. Multiple claims during the Policy Year are payable, but only up to the Base Sum Insured, which is available only once during the Policy Year. Cancer Booster is used last, after Base Sum Insured, Super Credit and Super Reload. It is renewable lifelong and renewal cannot be denied based on the previous year's claims experience.

user_query: Wheelchairs are listed as excluded under Prosthesis and Devices. Can I still claim one under the Durable Medical Equipment cover?
ground_truth_response: Yes, if the Durable Medical Equipment optional cover is in force. Wheelchair is on its list, and the cover states any exclusion under the Policy for the listed equipment does not apply to it. Conditions: the expense must relate to an admissible hospitalization under C.1, C.5 or C.6; the need must be prescribed during hospitalization or within 30 days post discharge; purchase/rental must be within 30 days of the recommendation; and claims reduce the Sum Insured.

user_query: Can I get Home Health Care paid on reimbursement if I arrange a nurse myself?
ground_truth_response: No. Home Health Care requires pre-authorisation and is not available on reimbursement basis. The services are provided through Network Providers / Empanelled Service Providers in select cities for select treatment procedures only. The treatment must otherwise require In-patient Care admissible under C.1, be prescribed in writing, and daily treatment records signed by the treating Medical Practitioner must be maintained.

user_query: I was admitted for 18 hours and then discharged. Will my claim be paid?
ground_truth_response: Only if the treatment qualifies as a Day Care Treatment. Hospitalization expenses are admissible only for a minimum of 24 consecutive hours, but this time limit does not apply to Day Care Treatments (procedures under general or local anaesthesia completed in under 24 hours due to technological advancement that would otherwise require over 24 hours' hospitalization). Treatment normally taken on an out-patient basis is not a Day Care Treatment.
verbatim_context: Expenses of Hospitalization for a minimum period of 24 consecutive hours only shall be admissible. However, the time limit shall not apply in respect of Day Care Treatments. [...] Undertaken under General or Local Anaesthesia in a hospital/day care centre in less than 24 hours because of technological advancement, and [...] Treatment normally taken on an out-patient basis is not included in the scope of this definition.
source_reference: Appendix A, Section C.1 Note a (Page 29); Section B.1 Definition 13 - Day Care Treatment (Page 2)

user_query: We just had a baby. Can we add her to the policy mid-term?
ground_truth_response: Mid-term inclusion is allowed only upon marriage or childbirth, and for a child, only after the child has completed 90 days and is less than 1 year of age, with additional differential premium calculated pro rata. Otherwise a child can be added only at the next Renewal (or start of the next Policy Year in multi-year policies). For any newly added member, the Pre-existing Disease clause, exclusions, loading and Waiting Periods apply afresh.
verbatim_context: Option of Mid-term inclusion of a Person in the Policy as an Insured will be only upon marriage or childbirth (inclusion of child only after completed 90 days and less than 1 year of age), Additional differential premium will be calculated on a pro rata basis. [...] Otherwise child addition can happen only in next Renewal or at the start of next Policy Year in multi-year policies. [...] the Pre-existing Disease clause, exclusions, loading (if any) and Waiting Periods will be applicable afresh for that member.
source_reference: Section E.2.5 Other Renewal Conditions b) (Page 19)

user_query: Would a diagnosis of carcinoma in situ of the breast trigger a payout under the optional Critical Illness Cover?
ground_truth_response: No. Critical Illness Cover pays for 'Cancer of Specified Severity', whose definition excludes all tumours histologically described as carcinoma in situ, specifically including Carcinoma in situ of breasts. (Note this is distinct from the Second Medical Opinion 'Cancer Treatment' definition, which includes in-situ cancer.)
verbatim_context: CANCER OF SPECIFIED SEVERITY [...] All Tumors which are histologically described as carcinoma in situ, benign, pre-malignant, borderline malignant, low malignant potential, neoplasm of unknown behaviour, or non-invasive, including but not limited to: Carcinoma in situ of breasts, Cervical dysplasia CIN-1, CIN-2 and CIN-3; [...] Any In-situ Cancer which is limited to the epithelium where it originated and did not invade the stroma or the surrounding tissues.

user_query: My oncologist recommends Cyber Knife radiosurgery. The policy covers 'Stereotactic Radio Surgeries' as a modern procedure. Is Cyber Knife covered?

user_query: ugh i literally bought this policy like 10 days ago and just broke my leg in a bike accident. ER + surgery. pls tell me im not stuck paying because of some waiting period??

The specific disease waiting period also doesn't apply to accident claims. Hospitalization (room, ICU, surgeon fees, OT, implants) is covered at actuals up to Sum Insured. For an emergency hospitalization, notify the insurer within 24 hours or before discharge, whichever is earlier; for cashless at a Network Provider, contact them within 24 hours of admission. Accident claims need an MLC/FIR copy.

user_query: my mom (58) has had diabetes for like 8 yrs. we just got her on Activ One MAX. if she gets admitted bcz of sugar issues will u guys pay or do we wait forever?

Options that change this: the optional Chronic Care (Day 1 In-patient Hospitalization) cover waives the PED waiting period and initial waiting period for listed chronic conditions including Diabetes, covering admissible hospitalization from Day 1 (subject to its premium grid/loading). Alternatively, the optional PED reduction cover can reduce the waiting period to 2 years or 1 year if opted at inception. Check the Policy Schedule for what's in force.

Diabetes [...] Option 1 - 3 Years to 2 Years [...] Coverage under the Policy after the expiry of months as specified in the Policy Schedule / Product Benefit Table of this Policy for any pre-existing disease is subject to the same being declared at the time of application and accepted by Insurer.

user_query: the hospital's bill has a bunch of random stuff — diapers, thermometer, food charges, 'misc charges'. my friend says insurance never pays for that junk. true??

Activ One MAX includes Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver), which covers non-payable items in all 4 lists of Annexure I when related to an admissible hospitalization claim. Diaper of any type, Thermometer and Food Charges (other than patient's diet provided by hospital) are in List I, and Incidental Expenses / Misc. Charges (not explained) are in List II. Confirm Claim Protect is mentioned in your Policy Schedule.

CHARGES (NOT EXPLAINED) [...] may be covered under this Product if Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver) is applicable to You and mentioned in the Policy Schedule.

user_query: my brother has been really struggling with depression and the doc wants him admitted to a psych facility. does the insurance even cover mental health stuff or is that excluded?
ground_truth_response: Yes, mental illness hospitalization is covered. Medical Expenses during Hospitalization arising out of a condition caused by or associated with medical illness, stress, anxiety, depression or a medical condition impacting mental health are covered at actuals up to Sum Insured.
